title.narrative: U: No. of positive quality audits carried out by national TVET body in the 9 target TVET institutions supported by the project

description.narrative: The indicator measures the number of positive quality audits carried out by national TVET body on 9 targeted TVET institutions supported by the project.The national TVET body refers to a national TVET authority from either ECOWAS, SADC or EAC country hired as external TVET qualified auditors to audit the TVET institutions in Liberia annually. Quality Audit is a process of checking or examining what goes on in an institution to ensure that there is institutional compliance with quality assurance procedures, integrity, standards and outcomes (National Council for Higher Education, 2014). Quality audit exercise verifies the presence of quality control mechanisms within the TVET institution and its effectiveness.The Quality Audit is based on 7 standard quality components namely quality management; management responsibilities; resources management (physical and human); design, development and revision of programmes; assessments and certification; and evaluation and improvement of quality. The 7 components cover a total of 22 assessment areas in the assessment form (See Table 3.1).

title.narrative: U: No. of TVET institutions rehabilitated and equipped with the support of the project by 2022

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of TVET institutions rehabilitated and equipped with the support of the project by 2022. The TVET Institution is considered rehabilitated when the building is completed and functional, hence the Take Over Certificate for completion of work is signed by the TVET institution, the Ministry and the project. The TVET Institution is considered equipped, when the equipment is supplied, installed and tested, after which a Goods Received Note is signed by the TVET institution. There is a possibility that a number of Goods Received Notes are signed because of different lots of equipment procured at different times. The TVET Institution is therefore considered equipped when the last lot of equipment is supplied, installed and tested, then the last Goods Received Note is signed. However, until the two documents (Take Over Certificate and Goods Received Notes) are not signed, the TVET institution cannot be considered rehabilitated and equipped.
